name: Matcha latte
caffeine: Caffeine comes from the whole leaf, higher than brewed green tea because you drink the leaf.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus, which print no tea: ask at lineup which teas the bar pours, and whether matcha and steamed milk are on hand.

what: Matcha whisked with a little water into a base of thin tea, usucha, then topped with steamed milk: a latte built on green instead of espresso. Matcha is shaded tencha leaf, dried flat, destemmed and traditionally stone ground, and it never dissolves. It is suspended, so the powder you whisk sets the strength, and it settles if left.
taste: Sweet grass and a savoury, seaweed-like weight under creamy milk, with a late, gentle bitterness. Unsweetened, most guests read it as grassy milk.

steps: Sift about 2 g of matcha into the cup.
Paste it with a splash of water around 175F (79C).
Add the rest of the water and whisk in a fast W until it foams.
Sweeten with syrup; granulated sugar will not go in.
Pour in milk steamed a shade under latte temperature.
make.ratio: 2 g matcha to 2 oz water, then 6 to 8 oz milk
make.dose: 2 g matcha, 2 oz water, 6 to 8 oz milk, syrup
make.cup: Warmed latte cup, or a tall glass over ice

serve: Out as soon as it is poured, since matcha settles; pour the milk into the green so any art sits on the base, and send a spoon. Iced, it separates, so walk it fast.
story: Matcha starts in the field, the bushes covered for weeks before picking to build chlorophyll and keep the sweet theanine. Ceremonial and culinary are marketing words with no law behind them, so buy on harvest date and taste it in milk. The calmer lift guests ask about is reported rather than proven, so say so.
guest: A matcha latte is powdered green tea whisked smooth, then topped with steamed milk: sweet, grassy and creamy. Let me check whether we have matcha tonight.
watch: Clumps mean the powder was not sifted or met milk dry: sift and paste it first.
Water at a boil pulls more bitter catechins: keep it off the boil.
Dull yellow-brown powder is old or heat-damaged.

recall.prompt: How is a matcha latte made, and what is in it?
recall.answer: Sifted matcha pasted with 175F (79C) water, whisked in 2 oz of water to a foam, sweetened with syrup, then topped with steamed milk in a warmed cup. Sweet, grassy and creamy.

quiz.q: Why does a standing matcha latte go gritty?
quiz.explain: Matcha is leaf ground fine and held in suspension, so it settles out; whisk late and serve at once.

quiz.q: About how much matcha makes one latte base?
quiz.explain: About 2 g, a level teaspoon, whisked into two ounces of water around 175F (79C).

quiz.q: What does ceremonial grade on a matcha tin guarantee?
quiz.explain: Ceremonial and culinary are marketing words that no law defines; buy on harvest date and taste.

video.label: Sifting and whisking matcha without clumps
video.watchFor: The sifting before any water touches it, and the fast W of the wrist rather than a circular stir. A matcha latte starts from the same whisked base, with the steamed milk poured in after.
